fragments.text: Hello, I'm Emil Petoras, and this talk is titled What Is The Test Group Bundle, Understanding the Race to Create Artificial General Intelligence. Billions of dollars are currently being poured into research projects to build artificial general intelligence, or AGI, defined roughly as any system capable of performing as well as, or better than, humans in every cognitive domain of interest. The two most notable examples are DeepMind, which is acquired by Google in 2014, and OpenAI, which has received $13 billion in funding for Microsoft. But why? What explains the billion dollar back to race to create AGI? The most obvious answer is profit. Microsoft and Google expect to make huge amounts of money from AGI. But this is only half the story.
fragments.summary: Hello, I'm Emil Petoras, and this talk is titled What Is The Test Group Bundle, Understanding the Race to Create Artificial General Intelligence.

fragments.text: The other half concerns a cluster of overlapping and interconnected ideologies that the computer scientist Timnay Gepprew and I call the test group bundle. The acronym test group stands for Transhumanism, Extropanism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Ultrism, and Long Termism. We don't need to discuss each of these ideologies here, though it would be useful to briefly explain Transhumanism, Effective Ultrism, and Long Termism. Transhumanism is a version of eugenics, which claims that we should radically reengineer humanity using advanced technologies to create a superior new race of post-humans. These post-humans could be immortal, superhumanly intelligent, and have perfect control over their emotions. Leading transhumanists include Nick Bostrom and Ray Kurzweil. fragments.text: Well, the other half is the test-grill worldview, according to which AGI will either usher in utopia or completely destroy us. As we should want to create utopia, we need to figure out how to build a safe AGI, though not everyone agrees that deep-mind and open AGI are developing their AIS systems in a sufficiently safe manner. Here it's useful to distinguish between two major camps within the test-grill movement, AI accelerationists and AI doomers. Both are in broad agreement about the ultimate goal, to re-engineer humanity, spread into space, overcome scarcity, and maximize value. What they disagree about is the probability of an existential catastrophe if AGI is created in the near future.

In Kalski, in fact, recently argued in the Pages of Time magazine that countries should engage in military strikes against data centers to prevent AGI, even at the risk of trickering in all-out thermonuclear war that kills billions of people.
